profile.name: Matthew De Jesus
profile.title: Power Electronics & Hardware Engineer
profile.tagline: MIT MEng candidate designing high-efficiency power converters, characterizing GaN devices, and building hardware from the transistor up.
about: I'm a Master of Engineering candidate at MIT working in the Research Laboratory of Electronics, where I design high-frequency PCB test platforms and characterize loss mechanisms in next-generation GaN power transistors. My work spans the full hardware stack — from custom resonant test boards and SCPI-automated instrumentation to the loss models that turn raw measurements into design insight.

I like problems where physics, circuits, and software meet. That has meant optimizing a synchronous buck converter to 97.8% efficiency with a Python design sweep, taping out a CMOS amplifier in Intel's 22nm process, pipelining a RISC-V CPU, and writing automation that makes lab measurements reproducible. I care about designs that are efficient, well-characterized, and actually buildable.
